children: The pharmaceutical company posts 24.9 per cent revenue growth and 38 per cent EBITDA growth in Q2 FY27, driven by strong performance in regulated and emerging markets

Senores Pharmaceuticals Limited reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA in the second quarter of FY27, with revenue rising 24.9 per cent year-on-year to Rs 192.3 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. The Ahmedabad-based pharmaceutical company also recorded its ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, supported by momentum across regulated and emerging markets, portfolio expansion and improved operational performance.

The company's EBITDA increased 38 per cent year-on-year to Rs 58 crore, while profit after tax (PAT) grew 22 per cent to Rs 37 crore. EBITDA margin expanded by approximately 290 basis points during the quarter.

For the first half of FY27, revenue increased 30 per cent to Rs 372.5 crore. EBITDA rose 58 per cent to Rs 111 crore, while PAT grew 31 per cent to Rs 67 crore. Cash generated from operations stood at Rs 38 crore, compared with Rs 31 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Regulated Markets remained the company's largest growth contributor, generating Q2 revenue of Rs 136.7 crore, up 27.9 per cent year-on-year. H1 revenue from the segment increased 34.3 per cent to Rs 264.5 crore. Senores expanded its Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) portfolio from 34 in September 2025 to 64 in September 2026. Of these, 23 products have been commercialised, while 41 launches are planned over the next 18–24 months.

Its CDMO/CMO pipeline comprises 41 molecules covering approximately 130 strengths. Emerging Markets revenue grew 21.2 per cent to Rs 38.4 crore in Q2, while H1 revenue increased 25.3 per ecnt to Rs 76 crore. Branded Generics revenue declined to Rs 9.5 crore from Rs 11.9 crore a year earlier.

The company is scaling up its Apnar facility, while upcoming contributions from Zoraya and Amerisyn are expected to support future growth. Initial operating and setup costs at these facilities affected profitability during the period.
Managing Director Swapnil Shah said the company remained focused on operational execution and portfolio expansion.

He added that anticipated scale-up from FY28 could improve operating leverage and margins. Senores expects 30–40 per cent revenue growth and 50–60 per cent PAT growth in FY27, followed by annual growth of 20–25 per cent over the next two years.
